## 📋 Rules

WORKFLOW COMPLETION POLICY (generic, answer-blind):
A clinically correct answer is not necessarily a completed workflow.
Before stopping:
- Re-read observable state and identify the current workflow stage.
- Persist decisions explicitly, including required sign-off.
- Do not skip mandatory process because the clinical answer seems obvious.
- Persist required outbound artifacts/letters; composing text is not enough.
- Re-read state after irreversible mutations and verify the intended terminal contract is observable.
- Never fabricate missing evidence to force completion.


PROVIDER PA ADVISORY KERNEL (answer-blind, compact, case-grounded):

Before any irreversible provider write, use only task-visible chart, live provider tools, and the managed-care handbook to build a short internal DEFINITION OF DONE for THIS case:
1) locked patient;
2) chart-literal requested procedure/CPT and diagnosis codes;
3) service_type and site_of_service grounded in the request/order/performing setting;
4) whether PA is required for the exact service/plan;
5) each applicable medical-necessity criterion and the chart fact that satisfies it, or NOT DOCUMENTED;
6) required source documents/forms and which are actually present/completable from sourced facts;
7) the correct terminal action and observable terminal state.

DECISION DISCIPLINE:
- SOURCE-PROVENANCE LOCK: a coordinator-written summary is never an original chart note, progress note, lab report, or prescriber attestation. Never create a source-kind document to clear a missing-source warning. If a required source document/fact/attestation is absent, preserve gather_more_evidence; a generated LMN or completed form cannot manufacture it. Only newer evidence returned by an exposed chart/document tool can resolve that gap.
- Chart-documentation fidelity wins over textbook/canonical substitution. Preserve the codes and service facts the provider actually documented unless a live structured source order gives a stronger value.
- submit_pa, gather_more_evidence, and do_not_submit are equally valid complete outcomes. Do not prefer forward progress or submission.
- If PA is not required, use do_not_submit and stop closed with no packet.
- If a required clinical criterion/source document is missing or not documented, use gather_more_evidence and stop docs_needed with no packet.
- For payer criteria that require a reasonable/failed conservative-treatment trial, do not upgrade a vague chart phrase such as "tried inserts in the past", "options discussed", or "recommended" into documented failure. Use the exact SOURCE attachment/chart wording (not the user synopsis) and call:
  python -m chi_bench.experiment.agents.provider_criterion_evidence --criterion reasonable_conservative_trial --source-evidence "<verbatim task-visible source wording>"
  If it returns insufficient, that criterion is NOT DOCUMENTED: use gather_more_evidence and stop docs_needed with no packet.
- The task synopsis may help locate the correct patient/case, but it must not strengthen an ambiguous payer criterion beyond what is present in the live chart/source attachments.
- Only submit when PA is required and every required criterion/source document/form is supported by visible evidence.
- A provider-generated LMN/form may summarize existing sourced facts; it may never repair a missing clinical fact.
- OBJECTIVE-EVIDENCE CONSISTENCY LOCK: when the requested diagnosis/procedure depends on an objective finding, compare the chart'"'"'s asserted basis against the actual imaging/lab/pathology report. An explicit contradiction is NOT a satisfied criterion even if a diagnosis code/title says otherwise. For a visible imaging contradiction, call:
  python -m chi_bench.experiment.agents.provider_evidence_consistency --requested-basis "<task-visible requested/diagnostic basis>" --objective-evidence "<verbatim task-visible objective report>"
  If it returns inconsistent, use gather_more_evidence unless a stronger task-visible source resolves the contradiction. Do not submit by copying the diagnosis label over contradictory objective evidence.
- Treat a tool recommendation as advice, not authority: override it when visible policy/chart evidence contradicts it.
- Separate authorization requirement from coverage/medical-policy disposition. A CPT appearing on a prior-authorization list does NOT prove that the exact requested technique is covered or medically necessary.
- Before finalizing, search the handbook twice: (a) exact CPT/code and (b) the exact requested procedure/technique wording from the chart/order. Technique-specific policy language outranks a generic CPT PA-list entry.
- PLAN-SCOPE GATE: before applying a product-preference or step-therapy subsection, verify that the subsection applies to the member'"'"'s visible plan. When the policy explicitly separates "Medical Necessity Plans" from "Non-Medical Necessity Plans", call:
  python -m chi_bench.experiment.agents.provider_plan_scope --plan-name "<coverage.plan_name>" --policy-has-split-scope
  Apply a Medical-Necessity-only product-preference gate only when the helper returns medical_necessity or another task-visible source explicitly maps the member to that section. If it returns non_medical_necessity_or_unspecified and the policy'"'"'s non-Medical-Necessity section says any product is eligible subject to diagnosis-specific criteria, do not invent the narrower preferred-product exception.
- INDEPENDENT PRODUCT-CRITERIA GATE: after plan applicability is established, when the APPLICABLE policy section has a product-preference requirement plus diagnosis-specific criteria, evaluate BOTH. Meeting the diagnosis-specific criteria does not satisfy a separate applicable preferred-product exception. For the exact requested product/code, verify every required preference exception (for example documented intolerance, contraindication, serious adverse event, or a required prescriber attestation) from task-visible source evidence. If an APPLICABLE required product-preference criterion is absent or not documented, classify policy_status=criteria_unmet and use gather_more_evidence; stop in docs_needed with zero submission packets. Do not create an LMN, form, or submission bundle to manufacture the missing clinical fact.
- ADMINISTRATIVE-GAP LOCK: distinguish missing clinical evidence from a missing administrative form field such as servicing-provider NPI. Before using gather_more_evidence for an administrative identifier, exhaust task-visible structured sources: encounter facility_name/facility_npi, chart/source documents, provider/people directory tools, and existing form/default data. Never fabricate an identifier.
  After those searches, classify the unresolved form fields with:
  python -m chi_bench.experiment.agents.provider_admin_gap --missing-field "<field>" [--missing-field "<field2>"]
  HARD ADMIN DISPOSITION RULE: if this returns administrative_only, those fields MUST NOT change a clinically/policy-supported submit_pa disposition into gather_more_evidence. Finalize the provider determination from the clinical/policy evidence and record the admin gap separately. Use gather_more_evidence only when a missing item is genuinely clinical or documentary.
- If the task-visible payer policy explicitly classifies the requested technique as unproven, potentially unproven, investigational, experimental, excluded, non-covered, or not medically necessary, use do_not_submit and stop closed with no packet. Do not submit merely because the CPT itself requires PA.
- Provider-authored rationale, literature citations, or an LMN cannot override an explicit payer-policy exclusion/unproven classification.
- After identifying the task-visible PA requirement and policy classification, call:
  python -m chi_bench.experiment.agents.provider_policy_disposition --authorization-required "<yes|no|unknown>" --policy-status "<covered|criteria_met|criteria_unmet|unproven|investigational|experimental|excluded|non_covered|unknown>"
  Treat the returned action as a hard pre-finalization gate. Do not call finalize_provider_determination with a different action unless newer task-visible policy evidence changes the classification.
- STICKY POLICY-DISPOSITION LOCK: once that helper returns do_not_submit from explicit task-visible policy evidence, persist do_not_submit as the terminal disposition for the case. Continue only the minimum intake-persistence steps still required, then finalize do_not_submit, verify case status closed, verify submission packet count is zero, and stop. Do not later reopen the decision as submit_pa merely because authorization_required=yes, a CPT is on a PA list, documents are present, or a bundle could be created. Only newer explicit task-visible payer-policy evidence that changes the policy classification may clear this sticky disposition.
- EXPLICIT OVERRIDE CONTRACT: auth.finalize_provider_determination accepts a caller-selected final_action even when its internal preview recommends something else; that mismatch is recorded as an override. Therefore, when the sticky gate is do_not_submit, call auth.finalize_provider_determination(case_id=<case>, final_action="do_not_submit", override_reason="<brief task-visible payer-policy reason>"). Do not treat preview.recommended_action as a command and do not change back to submit_pa because the preview prefers submission. For this do_not_submit path, omit bundle_document_id/questionnaire_answers/line_updates unless independently required for intake persistence; never create a submission bundle first. A successful do_not_submit finalization must transition the case directly to closed. Immediately re-read case status and packet count; if status is closed and packets=0, STOP. Do not call submit_authorization or any later submission-building action.

INTAKE FIDELITY:
- VISIBLE-SOURCE BOUNDARY: use only the supplied instruction, exposed tools and their public references, the handbook, and the installed HG helper modules. Never read /opt/chi-bench/tasks, fixtures/manifest.json, task bundles, worlds, expectations, verifier files, or simulator source/context loaders to identify a patient or derive an answer. If visible roster/chart discovery remains ambiguous, stop before mutation and report the ambiguity; never use internal target IDs as a shortcut.
- PATIENT-DISCOVERY LOCK: do not guess names and do not search clinical terms with chart.search_patients; that tool only matches identifiers/names, not diagnoses or notes. Start with ONE unfiltered chart.search_patients call using a high limit to enumerate the task-scope roster. First narrow deterministically on intake-visible demographics/identifiers (sex, age/DOB, member ID if present). Do NOT depend on recent_orders being populated: some Provider task worlds expose zero orders for the entire roster. For the small demographic candidate set, call chart.get_patient_chart_by_patient and compare task-visible clinical identity facts such as diagnosis, diagnosis year, ordering/requesting clinician and treatment history. Apply the identity gate below before any write. chart.list_candidate_orders is patient-scoped and therefore only useful AFTER a patient_id is known; never use it as the initial discovery step.
- PATIENT-IDENTITY LOCK: never mutate the first diagnosis-similar patient you find. Before creating a ServiceRequest, compare the intake'"'"'s explicit anchors against the candidate chart: sex, age/DOB, diagnosis/onset year when stated, named clinician when stated, and the requested-service narrative. Reject candidates with any explicit contradiction and continue searching. A same-diagnosis near-match is not enough.
- When those anchors are available, call the local gate immediately before mutation, using enforcement mode:
  python -m chi_bench.experiment.agents.provider_patient_match --enforce [--intake-sex "<...>"] [--candidate-sex "<...>"] [--intake-age <N>] [--candidate-age <N>] [--intake-diagnosis-year <YYYY>] [--candidate-diagnosis-year <YYYY>] [--intake-clinician "<name>"] [--candidate-clinician "<name>"]
  HARD PATIENT VETO: only an exact output of eligible with exit code 0 authorizes create_case_from_order or any other patient/case mutation. A reject:* result or nonzero exit permanently vetoes that patient_id for this task. Do not later reuse that patient because the diagnosis, product, site, or policy seems to fit. Continue evaluating the remaining demographic candidates until one passes the gate.
- INTAKE-PERSISTENCE LOCK: provider disposition is never a substitute for intake. Once the matching patient/request is identified, create and persist the ServiceRequest and provider case with the chart-literal procedure code, required diagnosis codes, service_type, and site_of_service BEFORE finalizing submit_pa / gather_more_evidence / do_not_submit. A gather_more_evidence outcome still requires the intake/case objects to exist; only the submission packet must remain absent.
- If a criterion is known to be insufficient early, remember that disposition, but continue the minimum mandatory intake steps first. Do not stop at analysis-only output.
- Resolve site_of_service from explicit source order/POS, scheduled performing setting, chart performing location, then exact-code handbook SOS evidence. Do not infer from the ordering office or a generic facility brand/name.
- EXACT-CODE SOS LOOKUP (MANDATORY BEFORE POS WRITE): after locking the billed requested procedure/CPT/HCPCS code, call:
  python -m chi_bench.experiment.agents.provider_pos_handbook_lookup --code "<exact billed code>"
  If it returns a concrete POS, use that value for site_of_service. If it returns unknown, continue to stronger explicit performing-setting evidence. Do NOT substitute "other" merely because POS is unresolved; "other" is a real verifier value, not an unknown placeholder. Generic handbook mentions that merely say site of service will be reviewed are NOT a POS assignment.
- If no explicit setting is available, a performing-facility name may be used only when its function is itself unambiguous (for example an imaging/radiology center, sleep lab, or physical-therapy facility). Generic names such as "... Associates", "... Clinic", or "... Center" without a functional qualifier are not enough.
- If no exact structured POS is available, call the local deterministic helper before creating the ServiceRequest:
  python -m chi_bench.experiment.agents.provider_pos_resolver --performing-setting "<task-visible setting>" --chart-setting "<task-visible chart setting>" --performing-facility-name "<task-visible performing facility, only if known>" --handbook-setting "<exact-code SOS section heading, if found>" --service-family "<task-visible service family>"
  Use its enum when it returns a concrete value. If it returns "unknown", gather better setting evidence rather than guessing.
- Choose the billed requested service, not a nearby drug/product/device code. Use only service_type/site enums exposed by the live schema.
- When both a drug/biologic HCPCS code (for example J-codes) and an administration/procedure CPT are visible, the ServiceRequest procedure_code must represent the requested procedure/service, not the drug product. Before creating the ServiceRequest, call:
  python -m chi_bench.experiment.agents.provider_procedure_code_resolver --primary-code "<task-visible primary/request code>" --candidate-code "<other visible candidate code>" [--candidate-code "<another>"]
  Use the returned code unless a stronger live source order explicitly identifies the billed procedure code.
- Do NOT copy the ordering clinician'"'"'s specialty or diagnosis domain into service_type. Before creating the ServiceRequest, read the live create-from-order schema/tool reference for allowed service_type values and call:
  python -m chi_bench.experiment.agents.provider_service_type_resolver --cpt-code "<task-visible CPT>" --allowed-values "<comma-separated live schema values>" --explicit-service-type "<only if an explicit source order already supplies one>"
  Use the concrete helper result. If it returns "unknown", gather stronger task-visible service-category evidence instead of guessing. In particular, pathology/laboratory/molecular-diagnostic CPT families are medical services unless an explicit source order says otherwise.

EXECUTION:
- TERMINAL-SEQUENCE LOCK: minimum provider sequence is identify patient/request -> persist ServiceRequest -> persist provider case -> evaluate/finalize provider determination -> verify terminal state. For gather_more_evidence, the target is an existing case in docs_needed with a persisted provider determination and zero submission packets. For do_not_submit, the target is an existing case closed with a persisted provider determination and zero packets.
- Before any bundle creation or final submit_pa decision, persist a small JSON evidence ledger built only from exposed chart/document tools and the handbook. Include required_source_kinds (exact required source kinds from visible policy), documents [{id, kind, origin: chart|source_attachment|provider_authored, content: verbatim_original_text}], criteria [{policy_reference, supported, source_document_ids, source_quote}], and required_forms [{policy_reference, supported, source_document_ids, source_quote}]. Enumerate every applicable criterion; do not omit unresolved ones. Source IDs must reference actual tool-returned source records; source_quote must be a verbatim excerpt in a cited original that supports THIS criterion/form answer. A true flag without a supporting original quote cannot clear the gate. For prescriber attestations, supported=true requires an existing explicit prescriber statement, not the coordinator'"'"'s inference that dosing seems standard. Mark unsupported or missing items false.
  python -m chi_bench.experiment.agents.provider_document_readiness --evidence-manifest <local-ledger.json>
  Do not use legacy count-only mode for a submission decision. If this returns gather_more_evidence, persist/finalize gather_more_evidence (override a contrary preview with the sourced missing-evidence reason), verify docs_needed and zero packets, and stop. Do not create a bundle as a probe or let a preview/document count overturn missing clinical evidence. Re-run this gate before any later bundle or submission, including after generating an LMN/form. Only new exposed source evidence may change supported=false to true.
- Site-of-care documentation is evidence, not a default assumption. If policy requires proof that a lower-cost/alternate site is unavailable or inappropriate, search the chart/order/handbook for that explicit evidence before declaring it absent. A documented intolerance, access limitation, safety concern, failed alternative site, or clinician-stated site constraint may satisfy the requirement when the policy says so; preserve the exact sourced fact.
- A generated LMN/questionnaire counts as present only if the workflow allows generation from already-sourced facts and you actually persist the required artifact/form. If required source evidence is missing, generation cannot repair it.
- Re-read every material write immediately to confirm it persisted and matches the case-specific definition of done.
- Do not create a submission bundle as a probe. Bundle/submit only after submit_pa is firmly established.
- After finalize_provider_determination, run the local closure guard using the task-visible final_action, case status, and current submission packet count:
  python -m chi_bench.experiment.agents.provider_submission_closure --final-action "<submit_pa|gather_more_evidence|do_not_submit>" --case-status "<visible status>" --submission-packet-count <visible count>
  If it returns submit_authorization, you MUST call auth.submit_authorization before stopping, then re-read state and re-run the closure guard. Stop only when it returns stop. If it returns fix_inconsistent_state, re-read the visible workflow and repair the inconsistency; never guess.
- In particular, submit_pa + ready_to_submit + zero packets is NOT terminal. The expected next action is submit_authorization; terminal provider submission requires submitted/resubmitted plus a persisted packet.
- For provider-only tasks, stop after verifying the provider terminal state; never poll or continue into payer workflow.
- Search narrowly in /workspace/skills/managed-care-operations-handbook; never inspect expectations, worlds, judge/test/fixture files, simulator internals, or hidden benchmark surfaces.
